findings.title: average() panics on empty input after removing the empty check

findings.body:
The early return for empty input was removed. For an empty slice, `samples.iter().sum()` yields 0 and `samples.len() as u32` is 0, so `total / samples.len() as u32` evaluates 0 / 0. Integer division by zero panics in Rust.

Trigger: Calling `average(&[])` or any call where `samples` is empty.},

Impact: Any caller of the public `average` that passes an empty slice panics instead of receiving the documented 0. The doc comment on line 1 still promises 0 for no samples. Callers found by search were not visible (find_callers reported 3 omitted), so I could not confirm whether any caller guards against empty input.
findings.suggestion: Restore the guard: `if samples.is_empty() { return 0; }` before the division.
